subject: Framework for GPU slab surge & burst policy — Halcyon AI procurement
body:
From: Aisha Khatri <aisha.khatri@halcyon.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@halcyon.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: clarification on surge guardbands and contracted burst

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement has a few follow-ups on the capacity model in the term sheet. Specifically we need to confirm:

- How burst capacity will be measured and billed (tokens, slots, or p99 sustained throughput)?
- Minimum headroom Redwood expects us to reserve vs. what can be provided as ephemeral burst.
- Autoscale cooldowns and pre-warming behavior for long-running chat sessions.

I've attached a small MAU/peak forecast for our expected rollout (halcyon_mau_forecast.xlsx). Our finance team will want a simple example showing cost at baseline reserved slab + two burst scenarios (30% and 100% uplift).

Can you loop in whoever owns the Dedicated autoscale policy and the ops constraints? We need language for the SLA and a sketch of the runbook for tech ops.

Aisha Khatri
Head of Procurement — Halcyon AI
procurement@halcyon.ai
Attachment: halcyon_mau_forecast.xlsx (xlsx)

----
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khatri <aisha.khatri@halcyon.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 Apr 2028 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: clarification on surge guardbands and contracted burst

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Rishi (SE) and Ben (ops) to address technical and operational constraints.

High level answers up front:
- Billing unit: we bill reserved capacity per vGPU-slab hour (committed). Burst is billed on incremental token consumption above the committed slab at a higher per-token rate; we can also model burst as ephemeral slabs billed per-minute for high-throughput periods.
- Headroom guidance: we typically ask customers to commit to a 1.25x baseline slab vs. median sustained usage for the first 90 days, then move to usage-based adjustments. For predictable launch programs, we recommend a short-term shoulder reserve (10–20% additional reserved slab) to reduce cold-start costs.
- Autoscale: default cooldown is 120s for scale-down, 30s for scale-up. For chat workloads with long-lived contexts we can pin prewarmed hosts for active sessions (session-aware prewarm) but that requires a small persistent shoulder.

I've attached a draft SLA that captures the above and some suggested billing examples (sla-draft-v2.pdf). Rishi, Ben — can you add sizing numbers from the MAU forecast and a proposed eviction / fallback policy?

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
Attachment: sla-draft-v2.pdf

----
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Aisha Khatri <aisha.khatri@halcyon.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 Apr 2028 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: clarification on surge guardbands and contracted burst

Hi all — I pulled the MAU forecast and sketched three launch scenarios (attached capacity_sizing_notes.xlsx):

- Conservative launch (week 1): baseline slab = 8 vGPU-slots, expected sustained throughput ~18k tokens/min, peak bursts up to 40k tokens/min for short windows (2–12 minutes).
- Growth launch (month 1–3): baseline slab = 12 vGPU-slots, sustained ~32k tokens/min, burst windows hitting 60–75k tokens/min.
- Full-scale (post-onboarding): baseline slab = 18 vGPU-slots with 1.25x headroom.

Autoscale recommendations:
- Scale-up threshold: sustained 65% utilization for 30s triggers an ephemeral slab add (1–2 vGPU-slots).
- Scale-down cooldown: 120s after utilization < 40%.
- Prewarm: enable session-aware prewarm for top 5% of long-running conversations (about 7% of concurrent sessions) — this reduces cold-starts and p99 latency by ~250ms.

Eviction/fallback:
- Primary behavior: graceful shedding via rate-limiter and user-level fair-queue weights when eviction required.
- Fallback variants: (1) route to lower-capacity quantized model (cost-effective), (2) route to hosted shared tier with transparent rate limiting.

Note on billing model alignment: I modeled burst as ephemeral slab minutes to keep invoicing simple for procurement — invoice line: Ephemeral slab minutes @ premium rate + incremental per-token over baseline. That gives finance a capped burst-dollar ceiling for defined windows.

Rishi Malhotra
Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
Attachment: capacity_sizing_notes.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Aisha Khatri <aisha.khatri@halcyon.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 Apr 2028 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: clarification on surge guardbands and contracted burst

Thanks team — operational constraints and clarifications from infra side:

- Headroom & prewarm: we can do a 10% shoulder reserve for the first 30 days at the customer's request; beyond that we need explicit reserved slab increases. Shoulder reserve is charged as reserved capacity but is refundable within 60 days with three business days' notice.
- Eviction policy: eviction is last-in-session, best-effort; we prefer graceful degradation (latency-based shed) to full disconnects. For compliance customers, we can provide a documented eviction trace in the audit logs.
- On ephemeral slab granularity: 1 vGPU-slot minimum for ephemeral adds, billed per-minute with a 2-minute minimum.
- Preemption: when cluster is under pressure, we will degrade non-critical background jobs and burst-only allocations before touching committed slab.

Operational ask for procurement: we need HALCYON to accept a SLA clause that allows automatic fallback to quantized model variants for transient overloads (these maintain output semantics for most endpoints but have a small variance in quality). We will also include an incident runbook and a contact rotation for on-call paging.

Internal link: runbook + playbook live at https://internal.redwood.ai/docs/dedicated-surge-playbook/halcyon (read-only for now).

Ben Carter
Head of Infrastructure Ops — Redwood Inference
Attachment: none

2) Accept the ephemeral slab billing model in principle; we'll need a simple example invoice line for our finance team that shows baseline, 30% burst, and 100% burst cost across a 24-hour window.
3) Schedule a 45-minute ops handoff call next Thu 10:00 PT to sign off on the runbook and on-call rotation. Can Rishi and Ben join?

Aisha Khatri
